issues.claim: Audit body §1: 'titles reading Milltown against a North Brunswick address'; email: 'the page titles still say Milltown'.
issues.problem: Only the homepage <title> says Milltown ('Lozito Law, LLC - Middlesex NJ Real Estate Lawyer - Milltown, NJ'). The About page <title>, reopened today, reads 'About Lozito Law, LLC - Real Estate Lawyer - Middlesex NJ' with no Milltown. The plural 'titles'/'page titles' is therefore inaccurate as written, even though the sitewide Yoast WebSite schema name ("Lozito Law, LLC | Middlesex NJ Real Estate Lawyer | Milltown, NJ") does still carry Milltown on both pages.
issues.fix: Write 'the homepage title (and the site name in its structured data) still say Milltown' in the body and the email, or 'the site still names Milltown'.

issues.claim: Opening line: 'Lozito Law has handled residential and commercial real estate from North Brunswick since 2013'.
issues.problem: The site supports the 2013 formation and the real-estate practice, and gives the current North Brunswick address, but nowhere states that the office has been in North Brunswick since 2013. A third-party listing still carries Milltown, NJ, so attributing the 2013 start to the North Brunswick address is an inference presented as fact.
issues.fix: Split the two facts: 'Lozito Law has handled residential and commercial real estate since 2013 and works from an office in North Brunswick'.

issues.claim: Audit body §3: 'the site answers none of the recurring closing questions'.
issues.problem: Absolute phrasing. The homepage does discuss inspection, appraisal and mortgage problems and says an attorney can 'successfully bring the transaction to closure'; it just gives no procedural answers (no FAQ, no checklist, no document list). 'None' overstates what was checked.
issues.fix: 'the site answers almost none of the routine procedural questions (documents, title commitment, signing)'.
